python3 << 'EOF'
import math

# Borrowing from the public - Federal securities (in millions)
# FY2016-FY2020 from 2020 bulletin (element 175)
# FY2021-FY2024 from 2024 bulletin (element 171)

data = {
    2016: 1419286,
    2017: 666472,
    2018: 1258348,
    2019: 1208690,
    2020: 4234396,
    2021: 1484000,
    2022: 2453245,
    2023: 2150233,
    2024: 2241060
}

# Verify we have 9 years
years = sorted(data.keys())
print(f"Years: {years}")
print(f"Number of data points: {len(years)}")

# Get values in fiscal year order
values = [data[y] for y in years]
print(f"\nValues (in millions):")
for y, v in zip(years, values):
    print(f"  FY{y}: {v:,}")

# Take natural log of each value
ln_values = [math.log(v) for v in values]
print(f"\nNatural log values:")
for y, ln_v in zip(years, ln_values):
    print(f"  FY{y}: {ln_v:.6f}")

# Calculate 20% trimmed mean
# 20% of 9 = 1.8, so we trim 1 value from each end (floor(1.8) = 1)
n = len(ln_values)
trim_pct = 0.20
trim_count = int(n * trim_pct)
print(f"\nTrim count from each end: {trim_count}")

# Sort the ln values
sorted_ln = sorted(ln_values)
print(f"\nSorted ln values:")
for i, v in enumerate(sorted_ln):
    print(f"  {i}: {v:.6f}")

# Trim from both ends
trimmed = sorted_ln[trim_count:n-trim_count]
print(f"\nTrimmed values (middle {len(trimmed)}):")
for v in trimmed:
    print(f"  {v:.6f}")

# Calculate mean of trimmed values
trimmed_mean = sum(trimmed) / len(trimmed)
print(f"\n20% trimmed mean of ln values: {trimmed_mean:.6f}")

# Round to nearest thousandths
rounded = round(trimmed_mean, 3)
print(f"Rounded to nearest thousandths: {rounded}")
EOF
